_note: FICTIONAL CREATOR PANEL (owner, 13 Oct). Every creator, brand, product, number, story and testimonial here is MADE UP for testing. No real person or business. Seeded by scripts/ops/seedFictionalPanel.mjs; run by scriptBatch.mjs --group=panel. Version 2: forty requests; each names the template (T1-T13) and duration profile it is meant to exercise, and `lacks` lists material deliberately missing so the writer must ask, not invent.

brand.name: Maya's Coffee
brand.description: A one-person small-batch coffee roaster selling beans online and at a weekend market (fictional).

voice.tone: warm, plain-spoken, a little nerdy about roast dates
voice.audience: people who brew coffee at home every morning
voice.summary: A small roaster who explains coffee without the snobbery.
voice.style_note: Warm, mid-length sentences, gentle nerdy asides about roast dates, says 'honestly' and 'here's the thing', talks to you, rarely exclaims.
samples: Here's the thing about roast dates. Honestly, the date on the bag tells you more than the fancy name on the front.
I check every batch by smell before it goes in a bag, which my neighbours find a bit odd. Honestly, it's the best test I've got.
If your beans taste flat, here's the thing: they're probably just old. Keep them in a jar, away from the light, and use them within a month.
You don't need a scale to start, you know. Honestly, a spoon and a little patience will get you most of the way.
Here's the thing nobody tells you about light roast. It wants hotter water than you think, and it rewards you for it.

stories.text: I started roasting in my garage with a secondhand popcorn popper, and the first batch set off the smoke alarm twice.
At my first market stall I sold out of Harbor Blend by ten in the morning and spent the rest of the day handing out samples from an empty table.
A regular told me her beans tasted flat after a week, and when I asked, she was keeping them in the fridge next to the onions.
I think most people who say they hate light roast have only ever had it stale.

products.offer: Harbor Blend, 12 oz bag, link in bio

facts.value: $17 for a 12 oz bag
12 oz whole-bean bag
Roasted on Tuesdays and shipped within two days of roasting

products.name: Night Owl Espresso
products.offer: Night Owl Espresso, link in bio

facts.value: $19 for a 12 oz bag
A darker roast pulled just after second crack, meant for espresso

answers.story: Here's the thing, a customer once brought back a bag because it smelled like toast, and honestly she was right, I had pushed that batch too dark.
answers.product_slot: Harbor Blend is a medium roast I make for drip and pour-over, honestly it's the one I drink every morning.
answers.niche: Here's the thing, I talk about home coffee, roast dates and keeping beans fresh, not latte art.
answers.profile: Honestly, I'm a one-person roaster talking to people who brew at home before work.

brand.name: Glow Lab
brand.description: A small skincare seller making a fragrance-free moisturizer and a cleansing balm (fictional).

voice.audience: people with sensitive skin who are tired of products that sting
voice.summary: A small skincare maker who explains ingredients plainly and avoids medical claims.
voice.style_note: Calm, careful, formal-leaning full sentences, no contractions, hedged ('in my experience', 'gently'), no exclamations, no slang.
samples: In my experience, sensitive skin responds best to fewer ingredients, not more. I would always patch test first, gently, on the inside of the arm.
I cannot tell you what your skin will do. What I can tell you is exactly what is in the jar, and why each ingredient is there.
Fragrance is added for the person shopping, not for the skin. In my experience, leaving it out is the kinder choice.
Please apply a small amount to damp skin and wait a moment. If anything stings, rinse it off gently and stop using it.
I test each batch on my own arm for a full week before it is sold. That is slow, and I am comfortable with slow.

stories.text: I made the first jar of the moisturizer in my kitchen because every store cream I tried left my cheeks red by lunchtime.
My first batch separated in the jar overnight, and I threw out forty jars before I got the emulsion right.
A customer emailed me a photo of her empty jar with a note that said she finally found one that does not sting.
I think fragrance is in most skincare for the shopper, not for the skin.

products.offer: Calm Cream, 50 ml jar, link in bio

facts.value: $28 for a 50 ml jar
50 ml glass jar
Fragrance-free, with no essential oils
Made in small batches of sixty jars
The first moisturizer that has not made my cheeks sting.
Launch price of $24 until the end of the month
$22 for a 90 g tin
90 g tin
A cleansing balm that rinses off with warm water

answers.story: In my experience, the first time I tested Calm Cream on my own cheek, I waited a full day before I trusted that it did not sting.
answers.product_slot: Calm Cream is a gentle, unscented moisturiser that I made for skin that reacts to almost everything.
answers.niche: I speak about sensitive skin, gentle routines and reading ingredient lists calmly.
answers.profile: I am a small skincare maker, and I speak to people whose skin is tired of stinging products.

brand.name: FlowDesk
brand.description: A small SaaS tool that turns a shared inbox into a simple task board for tiny support teams (fictional).

voice.tone: direct, practical, a founder talking to other small teams
voice.audience: owners of small online shops who answer customer email themselves
voice.summary: A solo founder building in public and explaining support workflows.
voice.style_note: Clipped founder talk, very short sentences, numbers, 'look', 'ship it', 'we', direct questions to the viewer, dry.
samples: Look. Your inbox is not a to-do list. Stop treating it like one.
We shipped saved replies on Tuesday. Took two days. Ship it, then fix it.
How many emails did you answer twice this week? Count them. We did. Forty-one.
Look, tags beat folders. Every time. We tested both.
Small team? Same five questions every day? Write the answer once. Ship it.

stories.text: I built the first version of FlowDesk over a winter because my partner and I kept answering the same customer email twice.
Our first paying customer found a bug in the first hour, and I fixed it on a call with her while she watched.
I once lost a whole Saturday to a support ticket that was really a typo in our help page.

products.name: FlowDesk
products.offer: FlowDesk free 14-day trial, link in bio

facts.value: $12 per month for up to three teammates
A shared inbox that turns each email into a card on a board
A 14-day free trial with no card needed

answers.story: Look. I answered every support email myself for a year. Missed a refund once. Customer waited a week. That's why we built FlowDesk.
answers.product_slot: FlowDesk sorts your shop inbox. Replies drafted. You approve. Ship it.
answers.niche: Small online shops. Customer email. Less time in the inbox.
answers.profile: Founder. Tiny team. We talk to shop owners who still answer email themselves.

brand.name: Coach Ana
brand.description: An online strength coach for beginners who train at home (fictional).

voice.audience: adults starting strength training at home with little equipment
voice.summary: A coach who keeps beginner training simple and safe.
voice.style_note: High-energy coach, short punchy imperatives, lots of exclamations, 'you've got this', 'one more rep', always 'you', some slang ('legit', 'gonna').
samples: Okay, you! Grab a chair. We're gonna do ten slow sit-to-stands. You've got this!
Legit, the hardest rep is the first one. Get it done and the rest is easy. One more rep!
Don't skip the warm-up, okay? Two minutes. That's it. You've got this!
Your knees go where your toes go. Simple! Gonna say it again: knees follow toes.
Tired? Good, that means it's working. One more rep, then you're done!

stories.text: The first time I tried a deadlift I copied a video and my lower back felt it for a week, which is why I teach the hip hinge with a broomstick first.
One of my first clients trained in a hallway with one pair of dumbbells, and we built her whole plan around that hallway.
I skipped warm-ups for a year and pulled a hamstring sprinting for a bus.
I think beginners quit because the plan is too big, not because they are lazy.

products.offer: Book a free 15-minute intro call, link in bio

facts.value: $90 per month
A weekly plan built around the equipment you already have
One video check-in call every two weeks

answers.story: My very first home workout I used water bottles as weights and dropped one on my toe, legit, and I still finished the set!
answers.product_slot: The Home Strength Starter is my beginner plan, bands and bodyweight, you're gonna do it right in your living room!
answers.niche: Strength training at home, beginners, little equipment, you've got this!
answers.profile: I'm a coach for adults starting out at home, no gym needed, one more rep!

brand.name: Clay & Kiln
brand.description: A home studio making hand-thrown stoneware mugs and bowls (fictional).

voice.audience: people who like handmade things for their kitchen
voice.summary: A potter showing the process behind each piece.
voice.style_note: Slow, long winding sentences with commas and dashes, sensory detail, gentle self-mocking humour, 'mind you', 'the clay decides', mostly 'I'.
samples: I sat at the wheel for most of the morning, mind you, and the clay decides when it is ready, not me, which is a humbling thing to learn at forty.
There is a sound a good pot makes when you tap the rim, a sort of low hum, and I have been chasing that sound for years, mostly in vain.
The kiln opens slowly, the way a parcel opens when you are not sure you ordered it, and half the time the glaze has had other ideas, mind you.
I made six mugs this week, and one of them leans like it has heard some gossip, so that one is staying with me.
The clay decides, really; I just keep my hands wet and try not to argue with it too loudly in front of the cat.

stories.text: My first kiln load came out with every mug glued to the shelf because I glazed the bottoms.
I threw the same mug shape about two hundred times before the handles stopped cracking in the kiln.
A buyer at a craft fair picked up a mug, turned it over, and asked why the bottom was not glazed, so now I explain it on every label.

products.name: Tide Mug
products.offer: Tide Mug, next batch drops in the shop, link in bio

facts.value: $38 per mug
Holds about 12 oz
Hand-thrown, trimmed and fired twice
Dishwasher safe, with an unglazed foot
$46 per bowl
Glazed in a green that pools darker at the rim

answers.story: I once opened the kiln to find a whole shelf of mugs had slumped sideways, mind you, the glaze came out lovely, so the clay decides, as ever.
answers.product_slot: The Tide Mug is a wheel-thrown mug with a soft blue glaze that pools at the bottom, a bit like the tide going out.
answers.niche: I make handmade kitchen pottery, mugs and bowls, mostly slow work at the wheel.
answers.profile: I'm a potter working alone in a small studio, making things for people who like handmade things in their kitchen.

brand.name: Signal Daily
brand.description: A short daily commentary channel on AI tools for working people (fictional).

voice.tone: skeptical, quick, explains why it matters
voice.audience: working professionals curious about AI tools but short on time
voice.summary: A creator who tests AI tools and says plainly what is useful.
voice.style_note: Rapid skeptic, rhetorical questions, 'so what?', 'the catch', 'real talk', second person, mid-short sentences, no hype words.
samples: New AI tool dropped. So what? Does it save you ten minutes on Monday or not?
Real talk: most of these demos are the best case. The catch is what happens on your messy files.
I tested it on a real spreadsheet. The catch? It invented two columns. So what does that tell you?
Do you need it? Probably not yet. Real talk, wait a month and see who still uses it.
So what changed? The price. That's the whole story, and the catch is the free tier.

stories.text: I asked an AI tool to summarize my own newsletter and it confidently quoted a sentence I never wrote.
I spent a week letting an AI assistant plan my calendar and it double-booked me on the one day I had a dentist appointment.
I think the most useful AI feature most people ignore is asking it to show its sources.

products.name: Signal Daily Newsletter
products.offer: Subscribe to the free newsletter, link in bio

facts.value: Free
One email every weekday with one AI tool tested

answers.story: Real talk, I once tested an AI tool that promised to save an hour a day, and the catch was it took an hour to set up.
answers.product_slot: Signal Daily is a short newsletter that tells you which AI tools matter this week, and so what for your job.
answers.niche: AI tools for busy professionals, minus the hype, what's the catch, what's useful.
answers.profile: I'm a skeptic writing for working people who are curious about AI but short on time.

answers.product_slot: Pip and Sprocket Live is our silly stage show, puppets, sound effects, and Sprocket says it is VERY serious!
answers.niche: Gentle absurd comedy, sketches, puppets, a lot of BONK.
answers.profile: We are a comedy duo, one human and one sprocket, for adults who like silly things!

brand.name: Pip and Sprocket
brand.description: A made-up puppet comedy duo that posts short sketches and plays a small live show (fictional).

voice.tone: silly, quick, warm, a little chaotic
voice.audience: adults who like gentle absurd comedy
voice.summary: A puppeteer and her grumpy robot puppet who turn small annoyances into sketches.
voice.style_note: Chaotic comedy, fragments, sound effects in caps, 'oh no', 'Sprocket says', lots of exclamations and questions, silly 'we'.
samples: Oh no. Oh no no no. Sprocket found the toaster again! BZZT. We are not doing this today!
Sprocket says the printer is a liar. Is he wrong? Is he? We'll never know!
BEEP. Who left one sock in the hallway? Sprocket says it's evidence. Oh no!
We tried to fold a fitted sheet. Sprocket says never again. Never! BZZT.
Oh no, it's Monday. Sprocket says Mondays are a bug. Can we report it? Can we?

stories.text: The first time I performed Sprocket live, his arm fell off mid-joke and the crowd laughed harder at that than at anything I wrote.
I rewrote our opening sketch on the train because a stranger told me the ending made her sad.
I once forgot the whole second act and Sprocket improvised a complaint about the lighting until I remembered it.
I think puppets let people laugh at things they would never laugh at if a person said them.

products.name: Pip and Sprocket Live
products.offer: Tickets for Pip and Sprocket Live at https://example.com/pip-live

facts.value: A live puppet comedy show with an audience sing-along at the end

brand.name: Quiet Loom
brand.description: A home weaving studio making wool scarves (fictional). Deliberately has no creator stories on file.

voice.audience: people who like handmade winter things
voice.summary: A weaver who has not shared any personal stories yet.
voice.style_note: Sparse and quiet, very short calm statements, present tense, 'slowly', 'thread by thread', no questions, no exclamations.
samples: The loom is warped. Slowly now. Thread by thread.
Grey wool today. It is soft. It is quiet work.
I pull the weft through. Slowly. The pattern shows itself thread by thread.
Winter light is short. I weave while it lasts.
One scarf a week. Slowly. That is enough.
